meta.title: Andrea & Jason's Wedding — What To Do Guide

1.label: Full Andrea
1.meaning: Sit, sip, stroll. Zero risk to the timeline.

2.label: Andrea
2.meaning: Easy and pleasant. Light effort, well-marked, predictable.

3.label: The Middle
3.meaning: A real activity, but you'll be fine. Bring water.

4.label: Jason-curious
4.meaning: Long, strenuous, or logistically ambitious. Plan ahead.

5.label: Full Jason
5.meaning: You might miss the wedding. Bring the headlamp you'll deny needing.

meta.scaleNote: The Andrea↔Jason scale measures sensibility / intensity, not just energy. Andrea = responsible, you make it to the wedding clean and uninjured. Jason = not entirely sensible, you might miss the wedding, it's 10 more miles than the sign said.

places.name: Rocky Mountain Arsenal National Wildlife Refuge
notes: An easy stop on your way in from the airport if you want to see some bison. We love it.
It's a beautiful place and not far from the airport — we actually filmed a music video here for some friends years ago.
places.verified: ~17,000-acre refuge on a former Army site; 330+ species incl. a bison herd (stay in your vehicle to view). Visitor Center at 7200 Quebec St, Bldg 121, Commerce City, CO 80022, open Wed–Sun 9a–4p. Free entry.

places.name: Caribou Hill (→ Bald Mountain)
notes: A great hike near Nederland through beautiful conifer forest — it's where Jason spends a lot of the winter on skis.
You can take it all the way up to Bald Mountain and get into the alpine this time of year.
You probably won't find many mushrooms, and maybe a stray raspberry in the boulder fields, but the fall colors on the way up are worth it.
places.verified: Caribou Hill ~3.4-mi loop near the historic Caribou Townsite; trail is poorly marked (carry GPS). Trailhead ~10,456 ft. Bald Mountain summit ~11,335 ft — this is the one in the Caribou/Nederland district.

places.name: East Portal / Moffat Tunnel hikes (James Peak Wilderness)
notes: The eastern portal of the Moffat Tunnel, where the Winter Park Express train disappears into the mountain. It's our gateway into the James Peak Wilderness — where we hunt mushrooms together and Jason skis.
Strenuous alpine bowls and cirques. Honestly, only attempt this if you're arriving early Thursday or Friday — go now and you might miss the rehearsal dinner. And bring the headlamp.
places.verified: From Rollinsville (4.5 mi south of Nederland on CO-119), take gravel Gilpin County Rd 16 west ~8 mi to the East Portal. Accesses Crater Lakes, Heart Lake, Forest Lakes, Rogers Pass, Rollins Pass and the Continental Divide Trail. James Peak Wilderness designated 2002.

places.name: Trail Ridge Road (scenic drive)
notes: Quite possibly the prettiest road in the country, and one of our favorites — aspens, maybe a moose, and high alpine you can't get to any other way.
It's a long drive all the way to Granby, so you might just go to the top and back.
places.verified: US-34, the highest continuous paved road in the U.S., crests at 12,183 ft; fully paved, two-way. Typically open late May through mid-October (snow-dependent). Alpine Visitor Center near the top sits at ~11,796 ft.

places.name: Old Fall River Road
notes: The dirt-road alternative to Trail Ridge — similar views, way less traffic, and most passenger cars are fine.
If you rent a bike in Estes it's a gorgeous gravel climb (~3,000–4,000 ft). The Jason version: ride up, bomb back down, slightly irresponsible, and extremely hungry at the end.
places.verified: ~9.1-mile, one-way, uphill gravel road (15 mph, no trailers/large RVs) from near Endovalley (~7,800 ft) up to Fall River Pass / Alpine Visitor Center (~11,796 ft) — ~3,900 ft gain over 16 switchbacks. Opened 1920. Open seasonally ~late June to mid-October.
places.ratingNote: Andrea version (drive) = 2. Jason version (ride up & descend) = 4.

places.name: Emerald Lake area (via Bear Lake Trailhead)
places.reservation: RMNP timed-entry + Bear Lake Road required
notes: Beautiful, popular hiking — we'd get in by 7am, since it's a long drive and it fills up fast.
places.verified: ~3.6 mi round trip, ~700–770 ft gain, passing Nymph and Dream Lakes en route to Emerald Lake (~10,110 ft). Very popular — go early. Requires the Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road permit in season.

places.name: Lost Lake (via Hessie Trailhead)
places.reservation: None — Indian Peaks Wilderness, NOT RMNP
notes: A real adventure — start early, the views are worth it. This is where we had our first kiss (over Himalayan leftovers), so it's a special one for us. Plan on a big day.
places.verified: ~4 mi round trip, ~1,000 ft gain, lake ~1.35 mi inside the Indian Peaks Wilderness boundary. This Lost Lake is in the Indian Peaks Wilderness, NOT inside RMNP — no RMNP timed-entry reservation required. Drive past Eldora Ski Resort; 2WD parking ends ~4.8 mi from the CO-72 turnoff, then walk the road to the Hessie footbridge.

places.name: St. Vrain Mountain & Meadow Mountain (via Ski Road)
notes: Our no-reservation way to technically walk into RMNP. Take Ski Road up Meadow Mountain, which connects over to St. Vrain Mountain — the summit looks straight down into Wild Basin with views of Longs and Meeker.
places.verified: From Allenspark, take Boulder County Rd 107 ('Ski Road') south ~1.5 mi, then NFS Rd 116.1 right ~0.5 mi to the trailhead (~12 cars). Meadow Mountain ~11,632 ft; St. Vrain Mountain summit ~12,162 ft, ~9 mi round trip, 3,000+ ft gain.

places.name: Middle St. Vrain Road / Camp Dick / Buchanan Pass (Peaceful Valley)
notes: A gnarly road — Jason took our Subaru Forester up it once and it's never quite been the same. It's our way into Buchanan Pass in the Indian Peaks Wilderness, the closest wilderness to the Denver metro. We come here for mushrooms and skiing.
places.verified: Middle Saint Vrain Trailhead at the west end of Camp Dick Campground, off Middle St. Vrain Rd (County Rd 92 / NFS Rd 114), ~6.5 mi north of Ward on CO-72. High-clearance 4WD can continue ~4 mi to the Buchanan Pass Trailhead.

places.name: Grand Lake water sports
notes: One of our favorite spots for hiking plus water sports — kayaking and SUP out on the lake.
places.verified: Grand Lake is the largest and deepest natural lake in Colorado, at the headwaters of the Colorado River on the western edge of RMNP. Outfitters (Mountain Paddlers, Grand Lake Marina) rent kayaks, paddleboards, and powerboats in summer.

places.name: Indian Peaks Wilderness (IPW)
places.reservation: None (USFS wilderness; some trailheads need day-use/parking permits)
notes: Just as impressive as RMNP, in our opinion — glacially carved and jagged. Ask Jason and he'll give you some exciting (read: ambitious) recommendations.
places.verified: Stretches from the southern boundary of RMNP south to the James Peak Wilderness, including the Continental Divide from Ogalalla Peak to Rollins Pass. No RMNP timed-entry required, though popular trailheads like Brainard Lake have their own day-use/parking permits in season.
places.ratingNote: Wide range — from Andrea-friendly approaches (2) to Full Jason objectives (5). Defaulted to 4 for filtering.

places.name: Cheese Importers
notes: A walk-in refrigerator room stocked with almost every cheese imaginable from around the world, plus an attached cafe.
One of our highly recommended stops — great for loading up on cheese for the weekend, especially if you're staying in Wicassa.
places.verified: Family-owned since 1976 at 103 Main St, Longmont, CO 80501. Largest walk-in refrigerated cheese & cured-meat market in Colorado (500+ varieties), with a Parisian-style cafe and a European housewares shop. Open Mon–Sat 9a–6p, Sun 11a–5p.

places.name: Kathmandu Restaurant (Nederland)
notes: The all-you-can-eat Himalayan spot. Go easy on the samosas — Jason learned that lesson the hard way here.
places.verified: Authentic Nepali/Indian/Himalayan restaurant at 110 N Jefferson St, Nederland, CO 80466, open since 1999; local favorite with a sister location in Boulder.

places.name: Crosscut Pizzeria and Taphouse
notes: Wood-fired pizza we love — just hard to get into.
places.verified: 4 E 1st St, Nederland, CO 80466. Neapolitan wood-fired pizza using organic Colorado-milled flour and a 3-day ferment; craft taphouse. First-come, first-served. Ranked #1 of 17 restaurants in Nederland.

places.name: Dry Storage
notes: A bakery and flour mill — part of a Colorado grain chain — with the best sourdough and croissants around. Jason sources our flour here.
places.verified: Bakery and grain mill by Id Est Hospitality at 3601 Arapahoe Ave (Unit D-181), Boulder, CO 80303. Mills its own locally grown grain and bakes bread and pastries from it.

places.name: Himalayan Curry & Kebob (Estes Park)
notes: This is the restaurant behind those first-kiss leftovers — so it means a lot to us.
places.verified: Nepali / Indian / Tibetan restaurant at 101 W Elkhorn Ave, Estes Park, CO 80517, on the main downtown strip. (A second Estes Park Himalayan option is Nepal's Cafe.)

places.name: Tarasco's
notes: Usually quiet, but it's great for vegetarians, vegans, and carnivores alike, with a specialty in mole. Our picks: the nopales, the banana-leaf tamale, and anything with mole.
places.verified: 470 S Federal Blvd, Denver, CO 80219. Authentic Michoacán cuisine — known for a seven-chile mole made with 30+ ingredients — plus a large fresh-juice bar. Open Mon–Sat 11a–9p, Sun 11a–8p.

places.name: O Lien Kitchen
notes: Hue-style Vietnamese — we love that they do a vegetarian Bún Bò Huế.
places.verified: Vietnamese restaurant at 781 S Federal Blvd, Unit B, Denver, CO 80219, on Denver's 'Little Saigon' stretch of Federal. Official spelling is O Lien Kitchen (two words).

places.name: Pho Duy
notes: Basically our second home — we're here every week and the staff knows us. Great vegetarian pho broth, maybe the best bánh mì in Denver, and tiny. (The restaurant photos on this site were taken here.)
places.verified: Vietnamese restaurant at 925 S Federal Blvd, Denver, CO 80219, on Denver's 'Little Saigon' stretch of Federal — a longtime local favorite for pho. (Internal nickname 'Fuzzy's' → official name Pho Duy.)

places.name: J's Noodles Star Thai 2
notes: If they're too busy they'll tell you to leave — and it's still some of the best Thai we've had anywhere.
places.verified: Tiny, cult-favorite Thai spot at 945 S Federal Blvd, Denver, CO 80219 (seats ~20). Known for pad thai, drunken noodles, and tom yum. Hours are limited/split — check before going.

places.name: Getting Here From the Airport
notes: Standard route: I-470 across the plains and into Longmont (nice) — but a little boring.
Alternate: 270 to 36 — it's fine.
Bike route: this is Jason's bike-from-the-airport option, which is exactly why it's so slow and weird.
Pick your stops and detours below depending on what time you land.

places.name: Scenic Drive to the Venue (Coal Creek Canyon → Peak to Peak)
notes: Take I-70 to Exit 6 (Golden), then Hwy 93 up Coal Creek Canyon, then the Peak to Peak Hwy down into Lyons. It's our favorite way in.
Stop in Nederland on the way — Kathmandu (all-you-can-eat), Crosscut, and Caribou Hill are all right there.

places.name: Rocky Mountain National Park Reservations Explainer
notes: RMNP requires reservations (timed entry). Here's the verified 2026 summary.
Required: daily May 22 – Oct 18, 2026, for entry 5:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Outside that window/season = no reservation needed.
Two permit types: (1) Timed Entry (park minus the Bear Lake Rd corridor); (2) Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road (whole park incl. Bear/Dream/Emerald Lake).
How it works: reserve a 2-hour entry window; once inside you can stay as long as you want.
Where & cost: all permits on Recreation.gov, $2 processing fee per reservation (on top of the park entrance fee).
Release schedule: bulk permits drop 8:00 a.m. MDT on the 1st of the prior month; a smaller next-day batch releases first-come at 7:00 p.m. MDT the evening before.

Workaround: enter before 5 a.m. or after 6 p.m. to skip the permit entirely. Or avoid RMNP reservations altogether by hiking in via the Indian Peaks Wilderness / Wild Basin from Allenspark (St. Vrain / Meadow Mountain).
Always re-check Recreation.gov / nps.gov/romo close to the date — exact 2026 dates can shift with conditions.
places.verified: Verified against current 2026 RMNP timed-entry system.

places.name: Estes Park (Friday morning)
places.reservation: RMNP timed-entry required for the park
notes: The gateway to RMNP and a great launch point for Trail Ridge Road, Old Fall River Road, Emerald Lake, and Himalayan Curry & Kebob (our first-kiss spot).
You'll need a park reservation — tap the permit flag for the details.

places.name: Grand Lake / Winter Park Vacation Loop
places.town: Lyons → Grand Lake → Winter Park → Denver
notes: Up Trail Ridge Road to Grand Lake, then Hwy 34 to Winter Park, then Hwy 40 down to I-70 and into Denver — or run it the other way. We love this loop.
Our pre-wedding version: a night in Grand Lake, a night in Winter Park, finishing in Estes (or flip it).
Hiking plus kayaking and SUP on Grand Lake.

places.name: Stop in Denver — Lil Saigon / Athmar Park
notes: A perfect stop on the way in or out. Lil Saigon (Athmar Park) is our neighborhood — and, we'd argue, the best food in Denver.
The district runs along Federal Blvd from Alameda to past Mississippi: Vietnamese, Mexican, and Thai.
Our standouts: Tarasco's, O Lien Kitchen, Pho Duy (aka 'Fuzzy's'), and J's Noodles Star Thai 2.
